BA.rationale: Boeing is in a genuine recovery phase with real operational progress — Q1 2026 revenue +14% YoY to $22.22B, operating income of $448M, and a balance sheet repaired from negative to +$5.99B equity. The $695B record backlog, FAA clearance to raise 737 MAX production to 47/month, and a 200-aircraft China order provide credible near-term catalysts. However, the company remains unprofitable at the net level (−$7M Q1 2026), cash-flow negative (−$179M OCF), and extremely leveraged at 7.84x D/E. Valuation is stretched — 75.7x PE on near-zero earnings, 1.3% earnings yield vs 4.47% risk-free — embedding substantial recovery that execution must validate. The 777X slipping into 2027 with 30 airframes needing rework and Spirit AeroSystems adding ~$1B negative cash flow in 2026 are material drags. The franchise (duopoly, backlog, services annuity) is above-average quality, but the margin of safety is thin until FCF inflects. Score reflects a mildly attractive franchise with improving trajectory, partially offset by extreme leverage, negative cash flow, and a valuation that prices in much of the recovery already.
